description: Fix email validation regex by creating a test runner and iteratively refining the pattern. TASK DETAILS: You have a workspace at /home/ga/workspace/email_validation with three files: (1) validator.py containing a broken EMAIL_PATTERN regex that is too restrictive, (2) test_cases.txt with 12 email test cases in format 'email | VALID' or 'email | INVALID' (8 should be VALID, 4 should be INVALID), and (3) README.md with instructions. YOUR GOAL: Create a test runner script (name it test_validator.py, test_email.py, run_tests.py, or similar) that reads test_cases.txt, parses each line to extract the email and expected result, imports and applies the EMAIL_PATTERN from validator.py, and reports which tests pass/fail. Then iteratively modify the EMAIL_PATTERN in validator.py and re-run your test script until all 12 tests pass. Finally, add at least 2-3 comment lines near the EMAIL_PATTERN in validator.py documenting what the regex matches and why. The test cases include edge cases like dots in usernames (john.doe@example.com), plus addressing (user+tag@domain.com), hyphens in domains (test-domain.org), multi-part TLDs (.co.uk), underscores, numbers, subdomains, and should reject emails with no username, no domain, spaces, or no TLD.
